result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers treat the supervisors' view as a hypothesis and center the plan on overnight drivers. B scores higher on sample design: it starts with 6–8 varied drivers, explicitly rules out a survey for now, writes neutral last-shift questions that avoid even the word 'voice', and gives more concrete access and safety steps. A has a strong ride-along and log plan, but it uses a larger sample, includes leading questions like 'when they last muted it and why', and is vaguer about getting sign-off and paying drivers for their time. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers treat the supervisors' view as secondhand and use the logs well. A fits the rubric better: it starts with a small, varied sample of 6–8 drivers, says outright not to run a survey first, and gives a fully neutral interview guide that avoids saying 'voice' until the driver does. B centres ride-alongs and lists strong hypotheses, but its sample is larger (6–8 ride-alongs plus 10–15 interviews) and it never writes out its questions, though it covers access and safety just as well.
